clue.text: Deputy’s role in recidivist’s scam?

blocks.note: a recidivist is on their second (or later) offence
a fiddle is a swindle or racket

explanation.surface: A habitual criminal's latest con is being discussed as if it were a job title.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: a repeat offender's racket would be a second fiddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing second fiddle means taking a subordinate supporting part, as an assistant or understudy does.

clue.text: Served up always with minimum of fuss, sauces less sweet?

definitions.note: a comparative adjective standing loosely for one meaning without sugar

indicators.note: in a down entry, serving something up lifts it so the letters read from bottom to top
the smallest possible portion of the word is just its opening letter

blocks.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever
the first letter of fuss
ragus are Italian meat sauces

explanation.surface: A dish is served promptly and without fuss, its sauces made with less sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole string EER + F + RAGUS is read upwards to give SUGAR-FREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something containing no sugar tastes less sweet, so the sauces described would carry the label for diabetic or dieting diners.

clue.text: Capital is sometimes available remarkably, resources initially raised

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words
in a down entry, raising letters lifts them so they read from bottom to top

blocks.note: something that is sometimes so can be so
opening letters of available, remarkably and resources

explanation.surface: A city's resources are remarkably available at times and are being raised.
explanation.walkthrough: CAN BE plus RRA gives CANBERRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Canberra is the seat of government of Australia, chosen as its capital city in 1908.

clue.text: Like a cheetah – with sharp teeth and claws?

blocks.note: first meaning: quick, speedy
second meaning: inclined to bite, snappy

explanation.surface: A description of a big cat, fast and armed with teeth and claws.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves describe a cheetah, so the clue looks like one definition; it is two senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippy means fast-moving, as the fastest land animal is, and also apt to nip or bite.

clue.text: Cruise: sense that’s inspiring where at sea

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the first word takes the second inside it
at sea means confused and adrift, so those letters are jumbled

blocks.note: to feel is to sense
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sea cruise, with someone sensing an inspiring place somewhere out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cruise' suggests ships, but the definition is the verb for coasting without power.
explanation.definitionFit: To freewheel is to coast along without pedalling or engine power, which is one meaning of cruising.

clue.text: Electrical device has to cross a channel for Spooner?

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the phrase is said his way

blocks.note: someone who crosses by swimming is a swimmer, and a channel is a ditch

explanation.surface: A gadget apparently needs to travel across the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of SWIMMER DITCH gives DIMMER SWITCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimmer switch is a control fitted to a light circuit to vary the brightness of the bulbs.

clue.text: Tea, it’s said, in bedtime drink

indicators.note: it's said means the word is to be heard, not read
in places the first piece inside the following word

blocks.note: the letter T is pronounced like tea
bedtime is late in the day

explanation.surface: Someone advises tea as the drink to have at bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bedtime drink' looks like one phrase, but drink alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is an espresso coffee made with plenty of steamed milk, served in cafés.

clue.text: See 5
Second article about evacuation of country cut

indicators.note: evacuating a word empties out its interior, leaving only its outside letters
about means surrounding, so the earlier pieces go round the next

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
the definite article
first and last letters of country

explanation.surface: A news report on a nation being evacuated, with a further article trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second article' is not a follow-up piece in a paper: second and article are separate pieces that wrap round the emptied country.
explanation.definitionFit: To scythe is to mow grass or crops with a long curved blade, so it is a verb for cutting.

clue.text: Ride in white vehicle

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the following one

blocks.note: wan means pale
a go is a turn or ride on something

explanation.surface: An invitation to take a ride in a white van or car.
explanation.walkthrough: White here means pale-faced, not the colour of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a wheeled cart or truck for carrying goods, a kind of road vehicle.

clue.text: Ultimately, storm in teacup brewing as American tires?

definitions.note: describes the tyres, so stands for an adjective

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very last letter of the next word
brewing stirs things together, so the collected letters are mixed up

blocks.note: last letter of storm
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A storm in a teacup brewing, with Americans growing weary of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tires' looks like the verb for wearying; it is the American spelling of tyres.
explanation.definitionFit: Pneumatic tyres are filled with compressed air, the standard kind on cars and bicycles.

clue.text: Some retro hairstyles returning shortly

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, sitting inside them
returning means going back, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the hidden run spans the end of hairstyles and the start of retro, read backwards

explanation.surface: Some old-fashioned hairdos are coming back into fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'retro hairstyles' backwards: selytsriahorter, which holds TERSELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tersely means in a brief, clipped manner, using few words, so it can be put as shortly.

clue.text: Temple guards at this spot, so there!

indicators.note: guarding something means surrounding it, so the first word goes round the next

blocks.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia
here means at this place

explanation.surface: Temple security staff stand firm at a particular spot, defiantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So there!' sounds like a childish retort, but it is a paraphrase of an old connective.
explanation.definitionFit: Whereat is an archaic word meaning at which point or thereupon, linking a result to its cause.

clue.text: Descriptive of some optical equipment, instrument with 5,7?

indicators.note: the answer at 7 is a word meaning swap, telling us to exchange letters in the other referenced entry

blocks.note: a horn is a brass instrument
the answer to 5 down

explanation.surface: A description of spectacles, plus an instrument tied to an earlier answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 5,7 is DIMMER SWITCH: switch the D and R of DIMMER to get RIMMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Horn-rimmed glasses have frames made of horn or plastic resembling it, a style of spectacles.

clue.text: Picture lover with jockey on top of Guernsey transported by cow?

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down entry is its first letter
something transported by a carrier is held inside it

blocks.note: to jockey for position is to vie
first letter of Guernsey
a cow is a mooer, one that moos

explanation.surface: An art lover rides a jockey atop a Guernsey cow being transported.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down entry 'on' puts VIE above G. A Guernsey is also a breed of dairy cow, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Pictures are films, so someone who loves them and goes often to the cinema is a moviegoer.

clue.text: Look of golfer regularly missing

indicators.note: missing letters at regular intervals leaves every other letter

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A golfer has an absent, out-of-form expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look' seems to be a noun about the golfer's appearance; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at someone openly and lecherously, a particular way of looking.

clue.text: Drudgery of the pig farmer?

blocks.note: surface reading: the hard menial labour involved in keeping pigs
setter's reading: pigs make low noises, so a pig farmer's work could be named after those sounds

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for menial toil starts with the noise a pig makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Grunt work is US slang for tedious, routine labour given to the lowest-ranking people.

clue.text: Air, in part, through American burner?

blocks.note: a carol is a song or tune
taken as written
an area is a part or region
per means by way of

explanation.surface: Some air passes through part of an American gas burner.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark tells us burner is playful: the thing burns your mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Carolina Reaper is a fiercely hot chilli pepper bred in South Carolina, so it burns.

clue.text: European lake drained

blocks.note: first meaning: Lake ..., an alpine lake in Slovenia
second meaning: past tense of a verb for drawing off fluid

explanation.surface: A lake in Europe has been emptied of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bled has had its fluid drawn off, like a radiator or a patient, so it is emptied.

clue.text: Put down ace and joker on deck and throw in one’s hand?

blocks.note: to bed is to plant or lay down
an ace counts as one
a wit is a joker
to deck someone is to hit them

explanation.surface: A card player lays down an ace and joker, then folds.
explanation.walkthrough: Ace, joker, deck and hand all set up a card game, but each word has a non-card meaning in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing in your hand means giving up, as does deciding to be done with it and stop.

clue.text: Number of suits and doctor eagerly embracing university student in America

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged
embracing means holding within, so the next word goes inside the previous one

blocks.note: a pack of cards has four suits, IV in Roman numerals
taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A keen doctor takes in a university, with a figure about suits mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ivy Leaguer attends one of the eight elite private universities of the north-eastern United States.

clue.text: See 17
See 18
Slump in queue for turkeys?

blocks.note: turkeys meet their end in December, abbreviated DEC
a line is a queue

explanation.surface: A slump in sales, with a queue forming to buy turkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: The queue for turkeys is the December line, ahead of Christmas dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A decline is a falling-off or downturn, just as a slump is a sharp drop in activity.

clue.text: Relic in rogue I love

blocks.note: a cur is a scoundrel
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to loving a villain, perhaps an old relic of a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A curio is a rare or unusual object kept as a curiosity, like an old keepsake or antique.

clue.text: Country with occupied territory fled by yours truly, cereal crop in blockade?

indicators.note: a place fled by someone no longer has them in it, so those letters go
something in a blockade is shut inside it, so the crop goes within

blocks.note: Crimea is the Ukrainian peninsula occupied by Russia
yours truly is the speaker, me
oats are a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A war-torn land: occupied territory abandoned, and its cereal harvest under blockade.
explanation.walkthrough: CRIMEA without ME leaves CRIA, which then holds OAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a nation in south-east Europe on the Adriatic coast, formerly part of Yugoslavia.

clue.text: Coach originally weighing a ton, not a car

indicators.note: originally points to how the word begins, its opening letter
not tells us to leave out the following letter

blocks.note: first letter of coach
something weighing a ton is heavy
the letter to remove

explanation.surface: A coach that weighs a ton is a bus, not a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Chevy is short for Chevrolet, a US car make.
explanation.definitionFit: Chevy is the informal name for a Chevrolet, an American brand of motor vehicle.

clue.text: New porthole battered, where it could be many times

definitions.text: where it could be many times

indicators.note: something battered is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new ship's porthole has been battered, somewhere it may have been many times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' sounds like occasions, but it means clock times.
explanation.definitionFit: Every time-zone line converges at the top of the Earth, so any clock time can apply there.

clue.text: As a unit, aware of fate in the end

indicators.note: in the end points to the last letter of the preceding word

blocks.note: to be in on something is to be aware of it
last letter of fate

explanation.surface: A group united, all aware of what fate has in store at the last.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in one means combined into a single whole, together, so it is a unit.

clue.text: Bread filled with something salty, though not a standard cheese

indicators.note: something filled with stuff holds it inside, so one word goes within the other
though not tells us that a letter is to be left out

blocks.note: bread is slang for money
tears taste of salt
the letter to remove
a jack is a flag, as is a standard

explanation.surface: Bread stuffed with a salty filling, though not a regular cheese sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is old slang for cash; a jack is a small flag flown at a ship's bow, just as a standard is a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Monterey Jack is a mild white Californian cheese named after the city of Monterey.
